title: Parallel Parenting Option Builder
tagline: Less parental conflict. Clearer boundaries. Greater stability for your child.
banner_title: Parent separately. Support your child together.
banner_body: Explore structured options for parenting when direct collaboration is difficult or inappropriate.
pdf_intro: Parallel parenting lets each parent care for your child in their own home and on their own time, with limited, structured and written contact between parents. These are the options you chose for your family.
pdf_closing: This plan is a planning tool, not a legal agreement or court order. If you have a court order, it always comes first. Review this plan with your attorney or mediator before relying on it.
disclaimer: Planning tool only - not a legal agreement or court order.

steps.title: Communication Boundaries
steps.short: Choose safe and effective ways to communicate.
steps.intro: Clear limits on how, when and what you communicate keep contact calm and predictable.

questions.text: How will you and the other parent communicate?

options.label: A co-parenting app only
options.desc: Written, time-stamped messages that are easy to review.

options.label: Email only
options.desc: Slower-paced and easy to keep as a record.

options.label: Text messages for logistics only
options.desc: Short, scheduling-only messages.

options.label: Through a third party
options.desc: A mediator, attorney or trusted person passes on information.

questions.text: When will non-urgent messages be sent?

options.label: One weekly update
options.desc: A single summary message each week.

options.label: Only when something changes
options.desc: No routine messages, just updates when needed.

options.label: Within set hours
options.desc: For example weekdays 9am-6pm, with replies within 48 hours.

questions.text: What topics will messages be limited to?

options.label: Child logistics only
options.desc: Schedules, health, school and activities. Nothing personal.

options.label: Child logistics and emergencies
options.desc: Plus urgent safety or medical matters.

steps.title: Parenting Time & Exchanges
steps.intro: A predictable schedule and low-contact exchanges help your child settle between homes.

questions.text: What parenting-time pattern fits your family?

options.label: Follow our court order exactly
options.desc: No changes without a written agreement or court approval.

options.label: Alternating weeks
options.desc: Fewer exchanges and longer stretches in each home.

options.label: 2-2-3 rotation
options.desc: Frequent contact with both homes, often best for younger children.

options.label: Weekdays in one home, alternate weekends in the other
options.desc: A steady school-week base.

options.label: At school or daycare
options.desc: One parent drops off and the other picks up, with no face-to-face contact.

options.label: A neutral public place
options.desc: Busy and well lit, such as a store parking lot.

options.label: A supervised exchange center
options.desc: Staff manage the hand-off for extra safety.

options.label: Curbside at a home
options.desc: The parent stays in the car while the child walks to the door.

questions.text: What happens if someone is running late?

options.label: Send a message at least 15 minutes ahead
options.desc: A short heads-up with a new arrival time.

options.label: 30-minute grace period, then reschedule
options.desc: After 30 minutes the exchange moves to the next agreed time.

options.label: Follow the court order's rules
options.desc: Use whatever your order already says.

steps.title: Decision-Making
steps.intro: Knowing who decides what removes many reasons to negotiate or argue.

questions.text: How will major decisions (education, health, religion) be made?

options.label: Split by area
options.desc: Each parent leads specific areas, such as one for school and one for medical.

options.label: Share in writing, then the lead parent decides
options.desc: Information is shared first and the designated parent makes the final call.

options.label: As set out in our court order
options.desc: Follow the decision-making terms already ordered.

options.label: With a parenting coordinator or mediator
options.desc: A neutral professional helps when you can't agree.

options.label: Each parent during their own time
options.desc: Meals, bedtime and screen time are up to the parent on duty.

options.label: Each parent, with a few shared basics
options.desc: For example the same bedtime and homework routine in both homes.

options.label: Each parent arranges activities on their own time
options.desc: No coordination needed.

options.label: Only activities agreed in writing in advance
options.desc: Especially ones that fall on both parents' time.

options.label: The child picks one activity per season
options.desc: Both parents support it during their own time.

steps.title: Information Sharing
steps.short: Share school and medical updates without direct contact.
steps.intro: Getting information directly from schools and providers means less need to talk to each other.

questions.text: How will you each get school information?

options.label: Each parent uses the school portal
options.desc: Grades, events and notices go straight to both of you.

options.label: Both parents listed with the school
options.desc: The school contacts each parent directly.

options.label: One parent forwards updates within 24 hours
options.desc: A short written forward, with no added comments.

questions.text: How will medical information be shared?

options.label: Each parent contacts providers directly
options.desc: Both parents are listed with the child's doctors.

options.label: Written summary after each appointment
options.desc: Facts only: what happened and any next steps.

options.label: A shared calendar for appointments
options.desc: Both parents can see what's booked.

options.label: Phone call right away, then a written follow-up
options.desc: Speed first, then a clear record.

options.label: Text right away with location and status
options.desc: Short and factual.

options.label: Through the agreed third party
options.desc: When direct contact isn't safe.

steps.title: Household Routines
steps.short: Respect each home's rules while keeping your child steady.
steps.intro: Children do well when each home is consistent, even if the two homes run differently.

options.label: Each home sets its own rules
options.desc: Children can adapt when each home is consistent.

options.label: A few core rules in both homes
options.desc: For example bedtime, homework and screen limits.

questions.text: How will clothes and belongings move between homes?

options.label: Two sets of essentials
options.desc: Fewer items travel and exchanges are quicker.

options.label: One travel bag that goes with the child
options.desc: Favorite items stay with your child.

options.label: A packing checklist shared before each exchange
options.desc: Fewer forgotten items and fewer messages.

questions.text: How will your child stay in touch with the other parent?

options.label: Scheduled calls at set times
options.desc: Predictable for everyone.

options.label: Child-initiated calls and messages
options.desc: Your child reaches out when they want to.

options.label: As set out in our court order
options.desc: Follow the contact terms already ordered.

steps.title: Changes & Disagreements
steps.short: Handle changes, holidays and disputes with a clear process.
steps.intro: A clear process for changes and disagreements stops small issues from becoming big conflicts.

questions.text: How will schedule changes be requested?

options.label: In writing, at least 7 days ahead
options.desc: Plenty of time to plan.

options.label: In writing, at least 48 hours ahead
options.desc: For smaller, one-off changes.

options.label: No changes unless agreed in writing or ordered
options.desc: The schedule stays fixed.

questions.text: How will holidays and special days work?

options.label: Alternate holidays each year
options.desc: Each parent has the holiday every other year.

options.label: Split each holiday in two
options.desc: Your child spends part of the day in each home.

options.label: Follow the court order's holiday schedule
options.desc: Use the holiday terms already ordered.

options.label: Go to a mediator before court
options.desc: A neutral professional helps you both reach a decision.

options.label: Ask a parenting coordinator
options.desc: Where one has been appointed.

options.label: 48-hour cooling-off, then a written proposal
options.desc: No same-day replies to disagreements.

options.label: Talk with my attorney
options.desc: Get advice before responding.
